description: We're Asmaa, Ruba and Aya, a team from Palestine. I'm Asmaa, a Computer Systems Engineering graduate from Birzeit University. We love turning real data into tools people can actually use, and we're excited to build with NASA's data.
summary:
Know Your Normal is a daily health self-check for astronauts on long-duration missions. Instead of comparing crew members with population averages, it learns each astronaut's own normal from their first 30 mission days and flags when they drift from it, because on long missions astronauts have to spot changes in themselves.

Each day the astronaut logs a quick check-in: resting heart rate, heart rate variability, blood pressure, sleep, mood, exercise, body temperature and dosimeter reading, plus an automatic emotion check from the real-time emotion analyzer built in Asmaa's graduation project. The app shows a green, yellow or red status for heart, bone and muscle, sleep, mood, immune and radiation, each with a clear next step and a report for the flight surgeon. An Isolation Forest also flags days whose overall pattern is unusual for that person.

In our simulated 90-day mission, it catches a heart-rate drift, isolation stress, missed exercise, a fever and a solar particle event, and the emotion check spots one astronaut's stress three days before his own mood rating does.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Know Your Normal helps astronauts on long missions evaluate and act on their own health. NASA's Human Research Program groups the risks of long missions into five hazards: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile closed environments. Our app turns a short daily check-in into a clear status for the body systems these hazards affect.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Daily check-in: resting heart rate, heart rate variability, systolic blood pressure, sleep, mood (1-5), exercise minutes, body temperature and the personal dosimeter reading.

2. Emotion check: the real-time emotion analyzer from Asmaa's graduation project at Birzeit University (ENCS5300) estimates eight emotions from a short check-in. It is an SVM + Random Forest ensemble on MFCC, chroma and mel-spectrogram features, trained on the RAVDESS dataset (83.7% accuracy on 8 emotions). The share of negative emotions becomes a mood indicator next to self-rated mood.

3. Personal baseline: mission days 1-30 define each astronaut's normal (the average and usual spread of every reading).

4. Rule check: the last 3 days are compared with that normal. Yellow ("Watch") at 2 standard deviations, red ("Act now") at 3, or when two readings in the same body system drift together. Fever (38 °C or more) and radiation spikes (4x the normal dose rate) turn red right away.

5. Pattern check: an Isolation Forest (scikit-learn) trained on each astronaut's own normal days flags days whose overall combination of readings is unusual, and shows which readings differ most.

6. Act: every status comes with a plain next step (go to the storm shelter, contact the flight surgeon, book a conference with the mission psychologist), plus a downloadable report, a crew board and a slider to replay the mission day by day.

DEMO

We simulated a 90-day mission for a 3-person crew with planted problems: a heart-rate drift (Cmdr. Lina), isolation stress with poor sleep and missed exercise (Eng. Karim), a fever (Spec. Maya) and a solar particle event for the whole crew. The app flags all of them, raises no status alerts during the healthy part of the mission, and the emotion check catches Karim's stress on day 61, three days before his own mood rating does.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

- Personal baselines catch changes that look normal for the population but are big for one person.

- It works on its own, without waiting for help from Earth, which matters when communication is delayed on deep-space missions.

- Every alert is explained: the reading, the astronaut's normal, and what to do next.

- The same approach could help people far from medical care on Earth, such as remote and isolated communities.

TOOLS

Python, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest), pandas, NumPy, Streamlit and Altair. The radiation status uses NASA's 600 mSv career limit from NASA-STD-3001. The emotion analyzer comes from Asmaa's graduation project, trained on RAVDESS.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It combines a personal baseline, an unsupervised pattern detector and an emotion analyzer, so behavioral-health changes can show up even when someone says they're fine.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

False alarms (alerts need a sustained change of 2-3 standard deviations), explainability, astronaut workload (one short daily check-in), and safety: the app supports the flight surgeon and does not replace them.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

The demo uses simulated data. Next, we would connect real wearable and dosimeter data, switch on the face module of the emotion analyzer, and tune the thresholds with flight surgeons.

USE OF SI

We used Claude (Anthropic) to help write the code, the simulated data generator, the text and the demo video. This is noted in the README, the code files and a watermark on the video.
